title: The length beneath the mat
subtitle: Min Ye's River Hen has brought rice and teak from Pegu. The granary men want the sacks now; a shipwright at the next landing wants to know why his two long planks are not on the declaration.

evidence.label: 01  Manifest
evidence.title: The River Hen’s declaration
evidence.text: Sixteen sacks of rice and eight planks of teak, all entered as short stock at 25 apiece. In the margin: 'Two planks have had their ends covered for the passage.' There is no separate line for long stock.

evidence.label: 02  Measure teak
evidence.title: The yard’s cord
evidence.text: The yard's long-stock cord spans twelve cubits. Six planks end at eight cubits; two continue under the folded matting and carry a straight, unjointed edge for fourteen. The clerk checks the earlier loading tally: the six short lengths and both long ones were all entered there before sailing, in that order. All eight planks are on deck for sale.

evidence.label: 03  Testimony
evidence.title: An untidy copy
evidence.text:
Min Ye: “The rice can go now; whatever you call these boards, the yard must send its own men.”

The clerk aboard: “I made the fair copy from the loading tally as the matting went on. I kept the total but copied the first line's description down the row.”

The shipwright: “I'll pay 25 for a short plank or 50 for one that takes the whole cord. I didn't see what was put aboard in Pegu.”

evidence.label: 04  Lift a binding
evidence.title: Beneath a frayed lashing
evidence.text: One of the bindings has left a dark line on the wood. A shave from the line comes away clean and the mark does not run into the grain. The underside shows no worm holes or soft patches.

rulings.label: Major Fraud — hold the suspect cargo
Story Event — hold the ship and notify the court

reasons.label: Two planks take the long-stock cord and match the loading tally; the short entry was copied over in error.
The dark line is worm damage, so the timber cannot sell as sound.
The matting conceals extra planks that were never brought forward for inspection.
Because the rice is sound, the timber declaration needs no change.

feedback_by_method.marks: The line left by a lashing is not a stock grade. It does not tell you where a plank ends.
feedback_by_method.testimony: The clerk tells you how he copied the tally, but you still need the yard cord to check which planks should be re-entered.
feedback_by_method.contents: The wood under the lashing is sound; that does not tell you whether it is short or long stock.
feedback_by_method.manifest: The declaration gives the right total. It repeats 'short' and never records the individual lengths.

hidden_truth.success: In the temenggung’s name, you enter six short planks and two long. Every piece matches the loading tally; the clerk copied the grade, not the lengths. The timber is worth 250 rather than 200, so three more in dues are payable when it lands. The granary men take the rice while Min Ye calls for the yard's crew.
hidden_truth.clear: You clear the River Hen as declared. The yard buys two lengths of long stock while the quay book values them as short.
hidden_truth.unsupported: The evidence cited does not support changing the declaration in the temenggung’s name. No additional dues are assessed.
hidden_truth.hold: You hold the River Hen and call the court. Its men find eight openly offered planks and a copying error. The timber and the rice miss the sale.

history_notes.note: Pegu supplied ship timber and rice to Melaka. Structural timber was plausibly sold by piece rather than by spice weight (docs/research/commodities.md, §§3.2–3.3; Pires, Suma Oriental, I, p. 195; Manguin 1980).
The 6% western customs rate is documented (docs/research/port-official.md). The two grades, their lengths and values, the yard cord, and the written manifest and tally are gameplay inventions.
